documents.description: The subclass 190 grants permanent residence indefinitely, but its authority to re-enter Australia lasts five years. To travel internationally after that, apply for an RRV with evidence of residence in Australia or substantial ties benefiting Australia.

documents.name: Australian citizenship by conferral application with residence evidence (Form 1300t)
documents.description: After meeting the general residence requirement (usually 4 years lawful residence including 12 months as a permanent resident), lodge with your Philippine passport, visa grant, PSA birth certificate and Australian residential/identity evidence. Philippine law generally allows re-acquisition of Filipino citizenship under RA 9225 afterwards — confirm with the Philippine Embassy in Canberra.

documents.name: Valid Russian international passport (заграничный паспорт)
documents.description: Original biometric travel passport. Must remain valid for at least three months longer than the temporary residence period being requested. Russian citizens enter Serbia visa-free for up to 30 days, so the passport is also the entry document.

documents.name: Scanned colour copy of the passport biodata page
documents.description: Digital scan of the photo/data page uploaded as an attachment in the eStranci online application (separate from presenting the physical passport at the police counter).

documents.name: eID.gov.rs electronic identity account
documents.description: Registered account on Serbia's Electronic Identification Portal, which is the mandatory login credential for submitting the temporary residence / single permit application on the welcometoserbia.gov.rs foreigners' portal. Single (residence + work) permit applications can only be filed electronically.

documents.name: Document proving the legal ground of residence
documents.description: One ground-specific document: employment contract with a Serbian employer, APR company registration extract (founder/director), notarized real-estate sale & purchase agreement, university enrolment confirmation, or marriage/family evidence. The chosen ground determines the rest of the file.

documents.name: Russian-issued civil status certificates (birth / marriage / divorce)
documents.description: Needed only for family-reunification or marriage-based grounds. Note: Serbia and Russia are bound by a bilateral legal-assistance treaty that in principle exempts public documents from legalisation, but many MUP offices still request an apostille — verify with the competent police administration before ordering documents.

documents.name: Certified Serbian court-interpreter translation of all foreign documents
documents.description: Every Russian-language document in the file must be translated into Serbian by a sworn court interpreter (sudski tumač). Translations are a separate deliverable from the original/apostilled document itself.

documents.name: Proof of sufficient means of subsistence
documents.description: Bank confirmation/statement showing funds at least at the level of the prescribed Serbian minimum salary, or a certified guarantee from an employer or household member with proof of their funds. Not required from immediate family members of Serbian citizens or from applicants applying on the basis of employment.

documents.name: Health insurance valid in Serbia
documents.description: Private health insurance policy covering the whole requested stay, or a valid Serbian RFZO health card once insured locally. Russia has no social-insurance agreement applicable for this purpose in practice, so a policy or equivalent proof of funds for emergency treatment is normally needed — same exemptions apply as for means of subsistence.

documents.name: Proof of payment of the administrative fee
documents.description: Receipt for the temporary residence approval fee (23,450.00 RSD; reduced to 11,725.00 RSD for marriage/extramarital union or kinship with a Serbian citizen). Payment must be made by card or by a payment order generated inside the portal, otherwise the application is not considered submitted. Russian citizens are not in the reduced-fee nationality group.

documents.name: Long-stay visa D
documents.description: Not applicable to most Russian applicants, who may enter visa-free for 30 days and apply for temporary residence from inside Serbia. Relevant only if the applicant chooses to obtain visa D at a Serbian diplomatic-consular mission first; in that case temporary residence must later be requested on the same ground as the visa D.

documents.name: White card — registration of address of stay (prijava boravišta)
documents.description: Address registration issued by the local police station, to be done within 24 hours of arrival. Hotels and licensed accommodation register the guest automatically; in a private flat the applicant must attend the police station with the landlord. Must exist before the residence application is decided.
documents.source: Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia (MUP), Department for Foreigners

documents.name: Lease agreement or landlord's notarized accommodation statement
documents.description: Document evidencing the Serbian residential address used for the application and for the white card. Distinct from the white card itself: this is the underlying private-law contract or owner's consent, not the police confirmation.

documents.name: Certificate of initiated procedure with foreigner registration number
documents.description: Confirmation issued after the application is accepted, showing the applicant's foreigner registration number (evidencijski broj stranca), which is needed by the applicant and employer to exercise rights and obligations in Serbia while the case is pending.

documents.name: In-person biometric data enrolment record
documents.description: Fingerprints, signature and facial image taken at the scheduled appointment at the police administration/office for foreigners. This replaces printed photographs for the card itself; minors under twelve are not fingerprinted.

documents.name: Serbian bank account opening file
documents.description: Account opened with the passport, white card and the foreigner registration number / residence decision. Practically required to receive salary, pay fees and evidence funds at renewal; exact documents differ by bank — verify with the chosen bank.

documents.name: Biometric temporary residence card or Single (residence and work) permit card
documents.description: The issued permit in the form of a biometric ID-style card, collected at the police station after the approval decision. The Single Permit variant also authorises work for applicants on employment or founder/director grounds.

documents.name: RFZO health insurance registration (M-A / employer registration)
documents.description: Enrolment into the Serbian Republic Health Insurance Fund once employed or self-employed, producing a Serbian health card that can later replace private insurance in the renewal file.
documents.source: Republic Fund for Health Insurance of Serbia (RFZO)

documents.name: Renewal application for temporary residence / single permit
documents.description: Filed through the foreigners' portal no earlier than three months before, and no later than the expiry date of, the current permit, with refreshed proof of ground, funds and insurance.

documents.name: Exchange of Russian driving licence for a Serbian one
documents.description: Available to holders of approved residence; typically requires the original licence, certified translation and a medical certificate. Deadlines and exact conditions vary — verify with the competent MUP traffic police department.
documents.source: Ministry of Interior of the Republic of Serbia (MUP)

documents.name: Permanent residence application file
documents.description: Submitted after three years of uninterrupted approved temporary residence; requires a registered residential address, proof of means and health insurance, and results in a five-year biometric foreigner ID card after new biometric enrolment.

documents.name: National Visa Application Form (Solicitud de visado nacional)
documents.description: One official Spanish national visa form per applicant, completed and signed; consulates specifically require fields for your US address/contact, intended date of entry, address in Spain, NIE, and full employer/company details to be filled in.

documents.name: Biometric passport-size photograph of the applicant
documents.description: Recent (within 6 months) color passport-size photo on photo paper, light/white uniform background, face fully visible, glued or clipped (not stapled) to the visa form. Some US consulates (e.g. San Francisco) ask for a second loose copy — verify with your consulate.

documents.name: Original valid US passport
documents.description: Unexpired US passport with minimum 1 year remaining validity and at least two consecutive blank pages; passports issued more than 10 years ago are not accepted, and the original is retained by the consulate during processing.

documents.name: Photocopy of passport biometric data page
documents.description: A plain photocopy of the passport page(s) containing the biometric/personal data, submitted alongside the original passport. This is separate from the loose biometric photograph.

documents.name: NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero) assignment
documents.description: Spanish consulates in the US require the applicant to obtain an NIE number before filing the telework visa application, since the number must be entered on the visa form. Requested through the consulate's separate NIE procedure.

documents.name: FBI Identity History Summary with US Department of State Apostille
documents.description: Federal criminal record check issued by the FBI within the last 6 months, apostilled (Hague federal apostille) by the US Department of State in Washington DC. State or local police checks and state apostilles are explicitly not accepted; do not remove apostille staples or seals.

documents.name: Sworn Spanish translation of the FBI criminal record certificate
documents.description: Certified/sworn translation into Spanish of the apostilled FBI record (consulates point to ATA-certified translators or Spain's official sworn translator registry). Other non-Spanish supporting documents generally also need official translation.

documents.name: Additional police certificates from other countries of residence
documents.description: Criminal record certificates from any country where you lived during the relevant look-back period (Washington DC states more than 180 days in the last 2 years; Houston states countries of residence in the last 5 years — verify with your own consulate). EU-issued certificates need no apostille.

documents.name: Responsible declaration of no criminal record (últimos 5 años)
documents.description: Signed sworn statement declaring absence of criminal convictions during the last five years, submitted in addition to (not instead of) the FBI certificate.

documents.name: Employer or client certificate authorizing remote work from Spain
documents.description: Letter from the non-Spanish employer confirming at least 3 months of seniority and express authorization to telework from Spain; self-employed/1099 applicants submit client contracts showing a relationship of at least 3 months and the remote terms of service.

documents.name: Certificate of company existence from the commercial registry
documents.description: Proof of real and continuous activity of the foreign (US) company: registry certificate or equivalent (e.g. Secretary of State certificate of good standing) showing incorporation date at least one year earlier and type of activity.

documents.name: Proof of professional qualification (degree or 3 years' experience)
documents.description: University or postgraduate degree from a recognized institution, professional/business-school certificate, or documentation of at least three years of relevant professional experience in comparable functions. Consulates may ask for homologation of foreign qualifications.

documents.name: Evidence of sufficient economic means (income and receipt of income)
documents.description: Documentation proving income above the statutory multiple of the Spanish SMI (plus an added percentage per accompanying family member): employment contract or company certificate stating salary, recent payslips or invoices, and matching bank statements showing the funds actually received. Exact euro threshold is updated annually — verify the current figure with the consulate.

documents.name: Private health insurance policy valid in Spain (full coverage, no copay)
documents.description: Health (not travel) insurance with an insurer authorized to operate in Spain, covering 100% of medical, hospital and outpatient costs with no deductibles, copayments, waiting periods or coverage caps, valid for the whole authorization. Not required if coverage by the Spanish public Social Security system is proven instead.

documents.name: Social Security undertaking: responsible declaration or US certificate of coverage
documents.description: Signed declaration committing to comply with Spanish Social Security obligations before starting activity, or — under the US–Spain totalization agreement — a certificate of applicable legislation/coverage issued by the US Social Security Administration. Consulate practice differs: some accept the declaration, others require proof of RETA registration or application — verify with your specific consulate.

documents.name: Proof of residence within the consular jurisdiction
documents.description: Document showing you live in the states served by the consulate where you apply, e.g. a notarized copy of a state ID, driver's license or student ID (Houston lists AL, AR, LA, MS, NM, OK, TN, TX). Required format varies by consulate.

documents.name: Visa fee payment receipt
documents.description: Consular visa fee paid in the form required by your consulate (e.g. money order payable to the Consulate of Spain); the reciprocity rate for US nationals is higher than the general rate. Confirm the current amount and payment method on the consulate's fee page.

documents.name: Certificado de empadronamiento (municipal registration)
documents.description: Registration on the Padrón Municipal de Habitantes at the town hall of your Spanish address, obtained after arrival using your passport, visa and a housing document (rental contract or property deed). Needed for the TIE, healthcare and most local procedures.
documents.source: Ayuntamiento (local town hall) – Padrón Municipal de Habitantes, Instituto Nacional de Estadística

documents.name: Spanish housing contract (rental agreement or property deed)
documents.description: Signed long-term rental contract or escritura for your Spanish address, used as proof of domicile for empadronamiento and often requested at the TIE appointment and for bank account opening.

documents.name: TIE application form EX-17 with Tasa 790 Código 012 receipt
documents.description: Foreigner Identity Card application submitted in person at the National Police / Oficina de Extranjería within one month of entry to Spain, with the paid 790-012 fee slip; appointment (cita previa) is booked through the sede electrónica and fingerprints are taken at that appointment.

documents.name: Spanish Social Security registration (alta / número de afiliación)
documents.description: Enrollment with the Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social before starting activity — self-employed applicants register under RETA, employees via their employer's registration — unless covered by the US–Spain totalization certificate.
documents.source: Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social (TGSS)

documents.name: Initial residence authorization for international teleworker (UGE-CE)
documents.description: Electronic application to the Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos for the 3-year telework residence authorization; the Washington consulate advises filing it about 2 months before the 1-year visa expires, proving the original conditions still hold.

documents.name: Spanish tax registration (Modelo 030) and optional Beckham-regime election (Modelo 149)
documents.description: Registration in the AEAT census of taxpayers once resident; international teleworkers may also elect the special non-resident tax regime (Ley Beckham) via Modelo 149, generally within 6 months of Social Security registration. Confirm deadlines and eligibility with AEAT or a Spanish tax adviser.

documents.name: Renewal evidence file (income, insurance and activity records)
documents.description: Maintained records for the 2-year renewal and later long-term residence: bank statements and invoices/payslips meeting the income threshold in force at renewal, continuous health/Social Security coverage, and evidence that Spanish-sourced work stays within the permitted minority share of activity.
documents.source: Unidad de Grandes Empresas y Colectivos Estratégicos (UGE-CE), Ministerio de Inclusión, Seguridad Social y Migraciones

documents.name: Valid Brazilian passport (passaporte brasileiro)
documents.description: Machine-readable Brazilian passport valid well beyond the intended landing date; the biographic data page is uploaded with the e-APR and passport details must match the Express Entry profile exactly. Brazil is a visa-required country, so the passport is also sent to the visa office for the permanent resident visa counterfoil.
documents.source: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) – Express Entry document checklist

documents.name: Language test results (IELTS General Training, CELPIP-General, TEF Canada or TCF Canada)
documents.description: Original test report from an IRCC-designated organization, less than 2 years old on the date of the permanent residence application. In Brazil, IELTS is offered in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Brasília, and CELPIP testing is available in São Paulo; French tests (TEF/TCF) are administered through Alliance Française centres.
documents.source: IRCC – Language requirements for Express Entry

documents.name: Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) report
documents.description: Report from an IRCC-designated organization (WES is the most commonly used route for Brazilian degrees) equating the Brazilian diploma to a Canadian credential. Must be less than 5 years old at the time of profile creation and of the application.
documents.source: IRCC – Educational credential assessment for Express Entry

documents.name: Apostilled Brazilian diploma and histórico escolar (academic transcript)
documents.description: Underlying academic documents issued by the Brazilian institution and apostilled under the Hague Convention (Brazil is a signatory; apostille is issued by authorized notary offices / cartórios under CNJ rules). These are sent to the ECA body, not to IRCC directly. Confirm the exact format your chosen ECA organization requires.
documents.source: Conselho Nacional de Justiça (CNJ) – Apostila da Convenção da Haia

documents.name: Certidão de Antecedentes Criminais issued by the Polícia Federal
documents.description: National criminal record certificate requested online at the Polícia Federal portal using CPF and RG/CIE, or in person at a PF office if you do not hold Brazilian ID numbers. IRCC no longer accepts Brazilian state-level certificates (Tribunal de Justiça / Secretaria de Segurança Pública) — only the national Federal Police certificate.

documents.name: Police certificates from every other country of residence (6+ months since age 18)
documents.description: Separate from the Brazilian Federal Police certificate: one certificate per country/territory where the applicant (and each accompanying family member 18+) lived six consecutive months or more since turning 18 — e.g. FBI Identity History Summary for the USA, ACRO for the UK, AFP National Police Check for Australia. Required only if such residence applies.
documents.source: IRCC – Police certificates for permanent residence applications

documents.name: Certidão de Nascimento (Brazilian birth certificate)
documents.description: Recent second-copy (segunda via) birth certificate for the principal applicant and for each dependent child included in the application; used to establish identity and family relationships in the e-APR.

documents.name: Certidão de Casamento, união estável declaration, or divorce averbação
documents.description: Civil status proof for applicants who are married, in a common-law/união estável relationship, divorced or widowed. A divorce must be shown by the certidão de casamento bearing the averbação de divórcio. Required only if applicable to the applicant's civil status.

documents.name: Employment reference letters from Brazilian (and foreign) employers
documents.description: Letters on company letterhead stating job title, NOC-matching duties, start and end dates, hours per week, annual salary plus benefits, and the signatory's contact details. Carteira de Trabalho (CTPS) entries, contracts and payslips can be attached as secondary evidence but do not replace the reference letter.
documents.source: IRCC – Express Entry: Work experience documents

documents.name: Proof of settlement funds — official bank letters
documents.description: Letters on each bank's letterhead (Banco do Brasil, Itaú, Bradesco, etc.) showing account numbers, opening dates, current balances, six-month average balances and outstanding debts, converted to CAD. Required for Federal Skilled Worker and Federal Skilled Trades applicants; Canadian Experience Class applicants and those with a valid job offer are exempt but must still upload a short letter of explanation because the checklist requests the item from everyone. Verify the current amount for your family size on the official IRCC table before submitting, as it is updated at least annually.

documents.name: Immigration Medical Examination (IME) results from an IRCC panel physician
documents.description: Upfront medical exam completed by an IRCC-designated panel physician in Brazil (clinics in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Brasília and other cities); the physician transmits results to IRCC via eMedical and gives the applicant a confirmation/receipt (IMM 1017B upfront medical report) to upload. Required for the principal applicant and all family members, including non-accompanying ones.

documents.name: Certified Portuguese-to-English/French translations with translator affidavit
documents.description: Every Portuguese document (police certificate, birth/marriage certificates, reference letters, bank letters) must be accompanied by a translation plus the original or a certified copy. In Brazil this is normally produced by a tradutor público juramentado; if the translator is not certified, a sworn affidavit from the translator is required. Confirm the exact certification wording with IRCC, as translation formatting is a frequent cause of incomplete applications.

documents.name: Confirmation of Permanent Residence (COPR) and permanent resident visa counterfoil
documents.description: Issued after approval. Because Brazilian citizens are visa-required, the visa office (Ottawa/Mexico City network serving Brazil) places a PR visa counterfoil in the Brazilian passport in addition to issuing the COPR/eCOPR; both must be presented to board the flight and at the Canadian port of entry.
documents.source: IRCC – Prepare for arrival as a permanent resident

documents.name: Signed COPR / eCOPR confirming landing
documents.description: At the port of entry (or through the PR Portal for in-Canada landings) the COPR is validated and signed; the signed eCOPR is the temporary proof of permanent resident status until the physical PR card arrives. Keep digital and printed copies — it is the document Service Canada and provincial offices will ask for.

documents.name: Personal effects accounting list (CBSA form BSF186) and 'goods to follow' list (BSF186A)
documents.description: Two typed copies of an itemized list, with values in CAD, of household goods brought at landing and of goods arriving later by air/sea freight from Brazil. Must be presented to CBSA at first entry to claim duty- and tax-free settler's effects; goods not declared at landing generally cannot be imported duty-free later.
documents.source: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) – Form BSF186 Personal Effects Accounting Document

documents.name: Currency declaration for CAD 10,000 or more (CBSA form E677)
documents.description: If cash, bank drafts or other monetary instruments totalling CAD 10,000 or more (including Brazilian reais at equivalent value) are carried in, the amount must be reported to CBSA at the border. Not a visa requirement, but non-declaration can lead to seizure of the settlement funds.
documents.source: CBSA – Cross-border currency and monetary instruments reporting

documents.name: Social Insurance Number (SIN) application at Service Canada
documents.description: Apply online or in person with the signed COPR (or PR card) plus the Brazilian passport and a Canadian proof of address. The SIN is not issued automatically on landing and is needed to work, open interest-bearing accounts and receive benefits.

documents.name: Canadian mailing address notification for the first PR card
documents.description: The first PR card is mailed automatically; if a Canadian mailing address was not given when PR status was granted, it must be supplied through IRCC's online address notification tool within 180 days or the card is cancelled and a new application with new fees is required.

documents.name: Permanent Resident Card (PR card)
documents.description: The official PR travel and status document, needed to re-enter Canada by commercial carrier (otherwise a Permanent Resident Travel Document must be obtained at a Canadian mission abroad). Renewals and replacements are made with form IMM 5444 under Guide 5445; keep a travel record because the 730-days-in-5-years residency obligation must be proven.

documents.name: Provincial or territorial health insurance card
documents.description: Apply with the COPR/PR card, Brazilian passport and proof of provincial residence (lease, utility bill). Coverage rules differ by province and some impose a waiting period of up to three months, during which private interim health insurance is advisable — verify the current waiting period with the provincial ministry of health.
documents.source: Provincial/territorial ministry of health (e.g. ServiceOntario–OHIP, RAMQ Québec, Health Insurance BC)

documents.name: Provincial driver's licence exchange or road test file
documents.description: The Brazilian CNH is generally usable only for a short grace period (often 60–90 days) after establishing residence, and most provinces do not have a full reciprocal exchange agreement with Brazil, so road and knowledge tests plus a certified translation of the CNH or an International Driving Permit are usually needed. Requirements vary by province — verify with the provincial licensing authority.
documents.source: Provincial licensing authority (e.g. ServiceOntario/DriveTest, SAAQ Québec, ICBC British Columbia)

documents.name: Nigerian international passport (biographical page)
documents.description: Current machine-readable Nigerian passport, valid well beyond the expected visa grant date, for the primary applicant and each dependent. The Department requires the biographical/photo pages of the current passport of every visa applicant to be uploaded to ImmiAccount. Renew early through the Nigeria Immigration Service if validity is short.

documents.name: Recent passport-style photograph of each applicant
documents.description: One recent colour passport-size photograph (head and shoulders, plain background) per applicant, uploaded as a digital image with the application. This is separate from the passport biographical page scan and from any photo taken at the panel clinic.
documents.source: Department of Home Affairs – Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) document checklist

documents.name: Nigerian birth certificate or NPC attestation of birth
documents.description: Birth certificate issued by the National Population Commission (NPC) of Nigeria for the applicant and each accompanying child, used to evidence age (points test) and identity. Where no NPC certificate exists, an NPC attestation of birth plus a sworn declaration of age is commonly submitted — verify acceptability with the Department, as evidentiary standards for Nigerian civil records are applied strictly.

documents.name: Sworn affidavit / change-of-name evidence for name discrepancies
documents.description: Nigerian court affidavit, newspaper publication or deed poll explaining any difference in name spelling or order across passport, academic (WAEC/degree) and employment records. Home Affairs requires evidence where a name has changed or differs between documents.
documents.source: Department of Home Affairs – Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) document checklist

documents.name: Positive skills assessment for the nominated occupation
documents.description: A suitable skills assessment issued by the relevant Australian assessing authority for your ANZSCO occupation (e.g. ACS, Engineers Australia, AHPRA-linked bodies, VETASSESS), valid at the time of invitation. Nigerian qualifications are assessed for comparability, so include the underlying degree certificate and academic transcript submitted to that authority.

documents.name: English language test result (IELTS/PTE/TOEFL iBT etc.)
documents.description: Test report showing at least Competent English, taken in the three years immediately before the invitation to apply. Nigerian citizenship does not exempt an applicant from testing (passport-based exemptions apply only to listed countries), and higher scores are needed for Proficient/Superior English points.

documents.name: State or territory nomination approval and SkillSelect invitation to apply
documents.description: The nomination decision notice from the nominating state/territory (issued after your SkillSelect EOI and, where required, a Registration of Interest) together with the invitation to apply. The 190 visa application cannot be lodged without an invitation tied to that nomination.

documents.name: Skilled employment evidence (reference letters, payslips, tax/pension records)
documents.description: For each period of claimed skilled employment in the 10 years before invitation: employer reference letters on letterhead stating position, dates, hours and duties, plus corroborating payslips, contracts, bank salary credits, FIRS/state tax documents or PenCom pension statements for Nigerian employment. Employment references must meet the Department's stated content requirements.
documents.source: Department of Home Affairs – Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) document checklist

documents.name: Nigeria Police Character Certificate (police clearance)
documents.description: Character certificate from the Nigeria Police Force Criminal Investigation Department, applied for through the POSSAP portal with fingerprint capture, for every applicant aged 16 or over who has lived in Nigeria 12 months or more in the last 10 years. Australian police certificates are treated as valid for 12 months from issue; if you are applying from outside Nigeria, allow extra time as the certificate is still issued from Nigeria.

documents.name: Additional overseas police certificates for other countries of residence
documents.description: Police/penal clearance certificates from every other country (including an AFP National Police Check for time spent in Australia) where any applicant aged 16+ has lived for 12 months or more cumulatively in the past 10 years — relevant for Nigerians who studied or worked in the UK, UAE, Canada, etc.
documents.source: Australian Federal Police – National Police Checks

documents.name: Immigration medical examination results via HAP ID at an approved panel clinic
documents.description: Health examinations (general medical, chest X-ray from age 11, HIV and serum creatinine/eGFR from age 15 for permanent visas) done only after you receive your HAP ID, at a Department-approved panel physician/clinic in Nigeria such as the IOM Migration Health Assessment Centres in Lagos and Abuja. Results are typically valid 12 months.

documents.name: Polio vaccination certificate
documents.description: Nigeria-specific requirement: applicants who have spent 28 days or more in Nigeria since 5 May 2014 should provide a polio vaccination certificate, ideally at lodgement and again at the panel physician appointment, or the case officer may request it and delay the application.
documents.source: Department of Home Affairs – migration health requirement (polio vaccination evidence)

documents.name: Form 80 (Personal particulars for assessment including character)
documents.description: Detailed 10-year history of addresses, travel, education and employment. Not always requested at lodgement, but commonly requested by case officers for applicants from Nigeria; preparing it in advance (with Form 1221 if asked) reduces processing delays.
documents.source: Department of Home Affairs – Forms (Form 80 / Form 1221)

documents.name: Relationship and family unit evidence for dependents
documents.description: Nigerian marriage certificate or registry/customary marriage evidence (or de facto relationship evidence such as joint accounts and cohabitation proof), children's birth certificates, and — for dependents aged 18+ — financial dependency evidence. Functional English evidence is also needed for each dependent aged 18 or over at lodgement, or the second-instalment VAC applies.
documents.source: Department of Home Affairs – Skilled Nominated visa (subclass 190) document checklist

documents.name: Visa grant notification letter (subclass 190) and initial entry date
documents.description: The electronic grant notice confirming permanent residence, visa grant number and the 'must make first entry before' date. Carry a printed copy plus a digital copy when travelling; Australia issues no visa label, and airlines/employers verify status electronically via VEVO.

documents.name: Tax File Number (TFN) application
documents.description: Apply online with the ATO once you have arrived and hold your permanent visa, using your passport/visa details; the TFN prevents being taxed at the highest marginal rate and is needed for employment and superannuation. If you already held a TFN on an earlier visa, keep the same number and update your details.

documents.name: Medicare enrolment (identity and residency documents)
documents.description: Enrol with Services Australia online via myGov or at a service centre using your passport with the permanent visa record plus proof of Australian residential address; documents are needed for each family member and do not need to be certified. Permanent residents receive a green Medicare card, usually posted within a few weeks.

documents.name: Australian bank account opening identity pack
documents.description: Passport, visa grant notice, TFN and Australian residential address details to satisfy 100-point identity checks for opening a transaction account for salary and rent. Requirements vary by bank; verify the accepted document combination with your chosen institution.

documents.name: Nigerian driver's licence conversion / state driver licence application
documents.description: Present your valid FRSC-issued Nigerian driver's licence with passport and proof of address to the road authority in your nominated state or territory. Nigeria is not on the recognised-country list for direct conversion, so knowledge and practical driving tests are generally required; deadlines to convert after becoming a permanent resident differ by state — verify with the relevant state road authority.
documents.source: Relevant state/territory road authority (e.g. Service NSW, VicRoads, TMR Queensland)

documents.name: Resident Return visa (subclass 155/157) for travel after five years
documents.description: The subclass 190 visa's travel facility expires five years after grant. To re-enter Australia as a permanent resident after that, apply for a Resident Return visa with evidence of residence in Australia (or substantial ties) — important for holders who travel frequently to Nigeria.

documents.name: Australian citizenship application evidence (residence, identity, police check)
documents.description: After meeting the general residence requirement (usually four years lawful residence including 12 months as a permanent resident), lodge a citizenship by conferral application with identity documents, residence evidence and any required police checks. Retaining Nigerian citizenship alongside Australian citizenship is permitted under Nigerian law for citizens by birth, but confirm current rules with the Nigerian High Commission.
